# Change Review

Apply the four lenses below in order. Answer each with evidence from the diff.
Report only what changes the author's next move; on a clean lens, say nothing.
Report the findings — don't edit the code.

Read the code around the change, not just the `+`/`-` lines. "Correct",
"simplest", and "root cause" all depend on what is already there.

```bash
git diff              # unstaged
git diff --staged     # staged
git diff main...HEAD  # branch vs trunk
```

## 1. Correctness

Ask: does it do what it intends without breaking what worked?

Look for:

- Logic errors — off-by-one, inverted condition, wrong operator.
- Unhandled cases — null, empty, errors, boundaries, concurrency.
- Broken contracts — a caller or test elsewhere this invalidates.
- Resource problems — leaks, unclosed handles, unbounded growth.

Give the input that triggers the bug and the wrong result.

Skip problems that already existed on untouched lines. Skip anything the
linter, type checker, or compiler reports. Skip nitpicks a senior engineer
would let pass. CI runs the build, types, and tests — don't.

## 2. Simplest to maintain long-term

Ask: is this the least code that solves the problem, and the version you would
want to inherit?

Look for:

- Config, flags, or layers for a case that does not exist yet. Delete them.
- A helper or dependency that repeats something the codebase already has.
- Cleverness that saves lines now and costs readers later.

Breaking changes are fine when they buy a cleaner result.

## 3. Root cause

Trace one level deeper. Ask: does it fix the cause or hide the effect?

Look for:

- A guard, retry, or `if` wrapped around a failure. Ask why the failure
  happens, and whether the fix belongs at another layer.
- A special case for malformed input. Ask why the input is malformed.

When the change treats a symptom, name the cause and where the real fix
belongs. When it is a deliberate stopgap, say so and name the follow-up.

## 4. Comments and prose

Ask: without this, would a careful reader get it wrong or get stuck? If no, cut
it.

Judge every comment, doc, commit message, error string, and log line the change
added or moved. Moved code brings its comments; they meet the same bar. Leave
the rest alone. Give one verdict per item, not one per file.

Code says what happens. A comment says why, or says nothing. When a comment
explains what the code does, make the code clearer and drop the comment. Cut
what stays down to the reason. Drop jargon a newcomer wouldn't know, or define
it once. Check the surrounding file for the same point made twice and keep one.

## Report

Group findings by lens, correctness first. For each: quote `file:line`, state
the problem in one sentence, give the fix. Close with the one change worth
making first.

# Codegraph — available (per-project; pass projectPath)

Codegraph is a SQLite knowledge graph of a codebase's symbols, edges, and
files: one `codegraph_explore` call returns the verbatim, line-numbered source
of the relevant symbols PLUS the call paths between them and a blast-radius
summary — replacing a grep + Read loop with one round-trip.

This server started somewhere with no `.codegraph/` of its own, so there is no
default project — but the tools are available and work **per project**:

- To query a project that HAS a `.codegraph/` index (e.g. a service inside a
  monorepo, or a second repo), pass its path as `projectPath` to
  `codegraph_explore` (and any other codegraph tool). Codegraph resolves the
  nearest `.codegraph/` at or above that path and answers from it — for as many
  projects as you like in one session.
- For a project with no `.codegraph/`, use your built-in tools (Read/Grep/Glob)
  for that project. Indexing is the user's decision — don't run it yourself, but

1	name: Cleanup PR image tag
2	
3	on:
4	  pull_request:
5	    types: [closed]
6	  delete:
7	
8	permissions:
9	  contents: read
10	
11	concurrency:
12	  group: cleanup-pr-image-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.event.ref }}
13	  cancel-in-progress: false
14	
15	jobs:
16	  cleanup:
17	    name: Cleanup PR image (${{ matrix.package_name }})
18	    # On `delete` events, only act on branch deletions (not tag deletions).
19	    # `pull_request: closed` is always in scope.
20	    if: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event.ref_type == 'branch' }}
21	    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
22	    permissions:
23	      packages: write
24	      contents: read
25	    # One leg per image that produces a handoff tag. `build.yml`'s matrix
26	    # pushes `pr-<N>` (or `branch-<ref>`) for both Linux images, so cleanup
27	    # must cover both — naming only one is what let `flutter-web` accumulate
28	    # an orphan per PR. `flutter-windows` is absent on purpose: `windows.yml`
29	    # calls `windows-image.yml` with `push: false`, so a PR builds it without
30	    # pushing anything to delete.
31	    strategy:
32	      # One image's cleanup failing must not skip the other's.
33	      fail-fast: false
34	      matrix:
35	        package_name:
36	          - flutter-android
37	          - flutter-web
38	    env:
39	      PACKAGE_NAME: ${{ matrix.package_name }}
40	    steps:
41	      - name: Harden runner
42	        uses: step-security/harden-runner@9af89fc71515a100421586dfdb3dc9c984fbf411 # v2.19.4
43	        with:
44	          egress-policy: audit
45	
46	      - name: Compute target tag
47	        id: tag
48	        env:
49	          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
50	          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
51	          REF_NAME: ${{ github.event.ref }}
52	        run: |
53	          set -euo pipefail
54	          if [[ "$EVENT_NAME" == "pull_request" ]]; then
55	            target="pr-${PR_NUMBER}"
56	          else
57	            target="branch-${REF_NAME//\//-}"
58	          fi
59	          # Defense in depth: fail closed if the computed tag does not match
60	          # the documented handoff-tag regex. Release tags (`<version>`) and
61	          # `buildcache` MUST be unreachable from this code path.
62	          if [[ ! "$target" =~ ^pr-[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ ! "$target" =~ ^branch-[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]]; then
63	            echo "::error::computed tag '$target' does not match handoff-tag regex; refusing to proceed"
64	            exit 1
65	          fi
66	          echo "target=$target" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
67	          echo "Computed target tag: $target"
68	
69	      - name: Resolve and delete GHCR version
70	        env:
71	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
72	          TARGET_TAG: ${{ steps.tag.outputs.target }}
73	        run: |
74	          set -euo pipefail
75	          # The package is user-owned (gmeligio); /user/packages/... is the

77	          # because the package -> repo Actions Access role is Admin.
78	          version_id=$(gh api \
79	            "/user/packages/container/${PACKAGE_NAME}/versions" \
80	            --paginate \

82	            | head -n 1)

84	          if [[ -z "$version_id" ]]; then
85	            echo "tag not found, nothing to delete (tag='${TARGET_TAG}')"

87	          fi
88	
89	          echo "Deleting version_id=${version_id} tag=${TARGET_TAG}"

name: Cleanup PR image tag

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [closed]
  delete:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: cleanup-pr-image-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.event.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  cleanup:
    name: Cleanup PR image (${{ matrix.package_name }})
    # On `delete` events, only act on branch deletions (not tag deletions).
    # `pull_request: closed` is always in scope.
    if: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event.ref_type == 'branch' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:
      packages: write
      contents: read
    # One leg per image that produces a handoff tag. `build.yml`'s matrix
    # pushes `pr-<N>` (or `branch-<ref>`) for both Linux images, so cleanup
    # must cover both — naming only one is what let `flutter-web` accumulate
    # an orphan per PR. `flutter-windows` is absent on purpose: `windows.yml`
    # calls `windows-image.yml` with `push: false`, so a PR builds it without
    # pushing anything to delete.
    strategy:
      # One image's cleanup failing must not skip the other's.
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        package_name:
          - flutter-android
          - flutter-web
    env:
      PACKAGE_NAME: ${{ matrix.package_name }}
    steps:
      - name: Harden runner
        uses: step-security/harden-runner@9af89fc71515a100421586dfdb3dc9c984fbf411 # v2.19.4
        with:
          egress-policy: audit

      - name: Compute target tag
        id: tag
        env:
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          REF_NAME: ${{ github.event.ref }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [[ "$EVENT_NAME" == "pull_request" ]]; then
            target="pr-${PR_NUMBER}"
          else
            target="branch-${REF_NAME//\//-}"
          fi
          # Defense in depth: fail closed if the computed tag does not match
          # the documented handoff-tag regex. Release tags (`<version>`) and
          # `buildcache` MUST be unreachable from this code path.
          if [[ ! "$target" =~ ^pr-[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ ! "$target" =~ ^branch-[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::computed tag '$target' does not match handoff-tag regex; refusing to proceed"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "target=$target" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Computed target tag: $target"

      - name: Resolve and delete GHCR version
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          TARGET_TAG: ${{ steps.tag.outputs.target }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The package is user-owned (gmeligio); /user/packages/... is the
          # authenticated-user endpoint. The workflow GITHUB_TOKEN can delete
          # because the package -> repo Actions Access role is Admin.
          version_id=$(gh api \
            "/user/packages/container/${PACKAGE_NAME}/versions" \
            --paginate \
            --jq ".[] | select(.metadata.container.tags[]? == \"${TARGET_TAG}\") | .id" \
            | head -n 1)

          if [[ -z "$version_id" ]]; then
            echo "tag not found, nothing to delete (tag='${TARGET_TAG}')"
            exit 0
          fi

          echo "Deleting version_id=${version_id} tag=${TARGET_TAG}"
          status=$(curl -sS -o /tmp/delete-body -w '%{http_code}' \
            -X DELETE \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer ${GH_TOKEN}" \
            -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json" \
            -H "X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2022-11-28" \
            "https://api.github.com/user/packages/container/${PACKAGE_NAME}/versions/${version_id}")

          case "$status" in
            204)
              echo "Deleted ${TARGET_TAG} (version_id=${version_id})"
              ;;
            404)
              echo "Version ${version_id} already gone (404); treating as idempotent success"
              ;;
            *)
              echo "::error::DELETE returned HTTP ${status} for version_id=${version_id}"
              cat /tmp/delete-body
              exit 1
              ;;
          esac

name: Cleanup PR image tag

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [closed]
  delete:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: cleanup-pr-image-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.event.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  cleanup:
    name: Cleanup PR image (${{ matrix.package_name }})
    # On `delete` events, only act on branch deletions (not tag deletions).
    # `pull_request: closed` is always in scope.
    if: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event.ref_type == 'branch' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:
      packages: write
      contents: read
    # One leg per image that produces a handoff tag. `build.yml`'s matrix
    # pushes `pr-<N>` (or `branch-<ref>`) for both Linux images, so cleanup
    # must cover both — naming only one is what let `flutter-web` accumulate
    # an orphan per PR. `flutter-windows` is absent on purpose: `windows.yml`
    # calls `windows-image.yml` with `push: false`, so a PR builds it without
    # pushing anything to delete.
    strategy:
      # One image's cleanup failing must not skip the other's.
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        package_name:
          - flutter-android
          - flutter-web
    env:
      PACKAGE_NAME: ${{ matrix.package_name }}
    steps:
      - name: Harden runner
        uses: step-security/harden-runner@9af89fc71515a100421586dfdb3dc9c984fbf411 # v2.19.4
        with:
          egress-policy: audit

`flutter-windows`'s Docker Hub page is never synced from `readme.md`. The
`update-description` job's matrix (`release.yml:185-187`) lists
`flutter-android` and `flutter-web` only, so a CI engineer landing on the
Windows image's Docker Hub page finds whatever is there by default, while the
other two images carry the project readme.

This is the same matrix omission that kept `flutter-windows` out of Docker
Scout ([#506]) — but where the Scout exclusion turns out to be correct on
technical grounds, this one is simply a gap. `peter-evans/dockerhub-description`
is an API call against a repository name; it has no Linux dependency and no
reason to skip a Windows image.

The spec layer has the same gap, and its shape shows where the fix belongs.
Description sync is specified **per image, in that image's own release
capability**: `web-image-release/spec.md:57` says "The Docker Hub repository
description for `flutter-web` SHALL be synced from `readme.md` on release, as
the Android image is." `windows-image-release`'s parallel requirement,
*Windows release uses the same metadata conventions as Android release*
(`spec.md:49`), covers registry namespaces, tags, and OCI labels — and stops
short of the description sentence its web counterpart carries.

Relevance gate: this changes what a CI engineer sees when they open
`hub.docker.com/r/<org>/flutter-windows` — the same project readme the other
two images show, rather than an empty page for the one image published by a
different job.

## What Changes

- `update-description` covers `flutter-windows`.
- `windows-image-release` gains a requirement for Docker Hub description sync,
  kept separate from its metadata-conventions requirement (`spec.md:49`).
  `web-image-release/spec.md:57` folds the same guarantee into its metadata
  requirement; that shape is not copied, because the two are observed
  differently — `docker inspect` versus a web page — produced by different
  actions in different jobs, and they fail differently. Bundling them obscures
  which one broke.

Explicitly **not** in scope:

- Declaring the published image set in a config file. Description sync is
  specified per image in each image's release capability, so the fix is one
  sentence in the capability that already owns the Windows image's metadata
  conventions. A declaration would be a different change with a different
  argument.
- `record-image`. Its omission of `flutter-windows` is correct and is handled
  by the `windows-scout-scope` change.
- `verify-published`, which already covers all three images
  (`release.yml:149-153`).

## Capabilities

### Modified Capabilities

The delta is purely additive — the capability gains a requirement; none of its
existing requirements are edited.

  the Windows image's registry presentation matches the Android and web images
  rather than stopping at OCI labels. Its existing metadata-conventions
  requirement (`spec.md:49`) is left untouched.

`:185-187`); `openspec/specs/windows-image-release/spec.md` gains a requirement
on archive.

repository must exist on Docker Hub and the `DOCKER_HUB_TOKEN` in use must be
able to edit its description, not only push to it. `peter-evans/dockerhub-description`

the leg, since `fail-fast: false` (`release.yml:183`) would leave a permanently
red leg reporting a fixable permissions problem as if it were a release
failure.

description is synced. That is existing behaviour for every image and is not

## Why

`flutter-windows` has never been analyzed by Docker Scout. The `record-image`
job's matrix (`release.yml:236-238`) lists `flutter-android` and `flutter-web`
only, so no Scout environment record or CVE SARIF is produced for the Windows
image and it is absent from the code-scanning dashboard ([#506]).

[#506] asks to verify whether Scout produces meaningful output for a Windows
image before wiring it up. It does not, on three independent grounds — each
one disqualifying on its own:

1. **Architecture.** Scout analyses `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` only
   ([docs](https://docs.docker.com/scout/policy/scores/)). The published image
   is `os: windows, arch: amd64`, read from its registry config blob rather
   than inferred. Not fixable: Windows containers are `windows/amd64` by
   construction.
2. **Size.** The same limit is 4 GB compressed. The published image is
   **5.90 GB across 37 layers**, the `servercore` base alone being 1.42 GB.
3. **No advisory data, and no inventory to apply it to.** Scout's 23 advisory
   sources include no Microsoft/MSRC feed, and every OS ecosystem it supports
   is a Linux one
   ([sources](https://docs.docker.com/scout/deep-dive/advisory-db-sources/)).
   Nor would another scanner help: `windows.Dockerfile` installs Git from a zip
   (`:20`), Flutter via `git clone` (`:42`), and VS Build Tools via an
   installer (`:74`). None is registered with a package manager, so an
   SBOM-driven scanner finds an empty inventory. Trivy's supported-OS table has
   no Windows row; Grype delegates cataloguing to Syft, which has no MSI or KB
   cataloger.

So the current behaviour is right and the omission is not a bug. What is wrong
is that nothing says so: the exclusion reads as an oversight, and the spec that
does mention it justifies it by the wrong thing (see below).

Relevance gate: this changes what a maintainer finds when they notice
`flutter-windows` missing from the code-scanning dashboard — a recorded
decision and a pointer to what does govern its CVE posture, instead of a gap
that invites the same investigation again.

## What Changes

- A new requirement in `windows-image-release` stating that `flutter-windows`
  is out of scope for Docker Scout, carrying all three disqualifiers with the
  source for each, making the exclusion conditional on those facts continuing
  to hold, and naming what governs its CVE posture instead: the `servercore`
  base-image digest pin (`windows.Dockerfile:3`) and the cadence at which it is
  bumped. That control is real and automated: Renovate's built-in `dockerfile`
  manager tracks the pinned digest — it needs no custom rule, since
  `.github/renovate.json` disables only the `github-actions` manager — on the
  weekly schedule the config inherits, with `automerge` enabled. Recent bumps:
  PRs #542, #435, #428, #425. Microsoft rebuilds Windows base images monthly on
  Patch Tuesday, and this repo picks those rebuilds up within the week.
- The existing *Manual `workflow_dispatch` rebuild is Windows-only* requirement
  is corrected. It currently justifies `record-image` skipping via
  `needs: release-android` (`spec.md:65`) — wrong twice over: no job named
  `release-android` exists (the code says `release-linux`, `release.yml:22`),
  and the skip is not produced by a `needs:` edge at all. Each downstream job
  carries an explicit `if: github.event_name == 'push' && !cancelled()` guard
  (`release.yml:181`, `:232`, `:284`), and under `!cancelled()` a skipped
  dependency does **not** auto-skip its dependents. The spec describes a
  mechanism the code does not use.
- A comment at `record-image`'s matrix recording the exclusion and its reason,
  so the omission is legible where someone would notice it.

Explicitly **not** in scope:

- Adding a Windows-capable scanner. Researched and rejected above.
- Any change to which images `record-image` actually records. Behaviour is
  unchanged; only its justification and legibility change.
- Declaring the published image set in a config file. That is a separate
  concern with its own defects to fix, and coupling it here is what made an
  earlier attempt at this change unreviewable.

## Capabilities

### Modified Capabilities

- `windows-image-release`: gains a requirement placing `flutter-windows` out of
  scope for Docker Scout on stated technical grounds; its
  `workflow_dispatch` requirement is corrected to describe the skip mechanism
  the code actually uses and to stop naming a job that does not exist.

## Impact

**Modified**: `.github/workflows/release.yml` (a comment at `record-image`'s
matrix, `:236-238`); `openspec/specs/windows-image-release/spec.md` on archive.

**No behaviour change.** `record-image`'s legs are identical before and after.
This change makes a decision legible and corrects a spec that misdescribes the
code; it does not alter what runs.

**Verification**: `record-image` runs on the next release with the same two
legs and the same SARIF categories. The spec correction is checked by reading
`release.yml:181`, `:232`, `:284` — the `if:` guards that actually produce the
dispatch skip.

**Risk**: low. The one judgement call is that the three disqualifiers are
durable. Architecture is structural; size has headroom in the wrong direction
(5.90 GB against 4 GB, and the image grows); the advisory-feed gap is
Docker's to close and would be announced. If Scout ever adds Windows support
the requirement should be revisited, not silently kept.

[#506]: https://github.com/gmeligio/flutter-docker-image/issues/506

`flutter-windows` SHALL NOT be recorded in Docker Scout, and the exclusion SHALL be justified by Scout's analysis support rather than by which job builds the image. The exclusion and its justification SHALL be discoverable by a maintainer reading the job that records images in Scout.

The exclusion SHALL hold only while all three grounds hold. If any ceases to be true, this requirement SHALL be revisited rather than carried forward unexamined.

The record SHALL name what governs the Windows image's CVE posture instead: the `servercore` base-image digest pinned in `windows.Dockerfile`, which Renovate tracks and bumps on the repository's regular schedule. That pin is the control a maintainer acts on, so the record SHALL point at it rather than leaving the posture unaccounted for.

The experience context is the maintainer who notices `flutter-windows` absent from the code-scanning dashboard. They find a stated reason and a pointer to the control that does apply, instead of re-opening an investigation that has already been done. Before this requirement the omission was indistinguishable from an oversight, and was filed as a bug.

- **AND** the reason cites Scout's platform and size limits and its advisory coverage, not the release topology
- **AND** each cited fact carries the source that establishes it

- **GIVEN** `flutter-windows` is out of scope for Docker Scout
- **WHEN** a release publishes it
- **THEN** its anonymous-pull verification is unaffected, as `ci-image-anonymous-availability` specifies

- **THEN** Android images are published at all three registries
- **AND** the workflow run is reported as failed (because at least one job failed)
- **AND** the failure surface is the `release-windows` job specifically, not `release-android`

### Requirement: Windows release uses the same metadata conventions as Android release

The Windows release build SHALL use `docker/metadata-action` with the `images` input set to the same three registry namespaces and the `tags` input set to `type=raw,value=${{ env.FLUTTER_VERSION }}`, mirroring the Android job. This metadata step runs inside the reusable `windows-image.yml` workflow invoked by the `release-windows` caller. The image labels (`org.opencontainers.image.*`) produced by `metadata-action` SHALL be applied to the built image (as `--label` arguments to `docker build`), so that `docker inspect` reports the same OCI label set as the Android image. `docker/build-push-action` is not a viable mechanism here because it does not support Windows containers (tracked at https://github.com/docker/build-push-action/issues/18).

The experience context is the operator inspecting `docker inspect <org>/flutter-windows:X.Y.Z` and `docker inspect <org>/flutter-android:X.Y.Z` and finding the same set of OCI labels (description, source, revision, version) populated with the same values.

#### Scenario: Labels match Android conventions

- **GIVEN** a successful `release-windows` run for tag `X.Y.Z`
- **WHEN** an operator runs `docker inspect docker.io/<org>/flutter-windows:X.Y.Z` and inspects the `Labels` map
- **THEN** the keys `org.opencontainers.image.source`, `org.opencontainers.image.revision`, `org.opencontainers.image.version`, and `org.opencontainers.image.title` are all present
- **AND** `org.opencontainers.image.version` equals `X.Y.Z`
- **AND** `org.opencontainers.image.revision` equals the commit SHA of the tag

### Requirement: Manual `workflow_dispatch` rebuild is Windows-only

The `release.yml` workflow SHALL continue to declare `workflow_dispatch:`. On `workflow_dispatch`, only the `release-windows` caller job SHALL execute; `release-android` and its downstream jobs (`update-description`, `record-image`, `create-github-release`) SHALL be skipped via an `if: github.event_name == 'push'` guard on `release-android` (the downstream jobs auto-skip via their existing `needs: release-android`). The experience context is the maintainer recovering from a transient Windows runner failure: they re-run the workflow on the existing tag instead of force-pushing a new one. Android recovery, by contrast, is the established fix-forward + re-tag pattern and does not need a `workflow_dispatch` path.

name: Cleanup PR image tag

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [closed]
  delete:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: cleanup-pr-image-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.event.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  cleanup:
    name: Cleanup PR image (${{ matrix.package_name }})
    # On `delete` events, only act on branch deletions (not tag deletions).
    # `pull_request: closed` is always in scope.
    if: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event.ref_type == 'branch' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:
      packages: write
      contents: read
    # One leg per image that produces a handoff tag. `build.yml`'s matrix
    # pushes `pr-<N>` (or `branch-<ref>`) for both Linux images, so cleanup
    # must cover both — naming only one is what let `flutter-web` accumulate
    # an orphan per PR. `flutter-windows` is absent on purpose: `windows.yml`
    # calls `windows-image.yml` with `push: false`, so a PR builds it without
    # pushing anything to delete.
    strategy:
      # One image's cleanup failing must not skip the other's.
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        package_name:
          - flutter-android
          - flutter-web
    env:
      PACKAGE_NAME: ${{ matrix.package_name }}
    steps:
      - name: Harden runner
        uses: step-security/harden-runner@9af89fc71515a100421586dfdb3dc9c984fbf411 # v2.19.4
        with:
          egress-policy: audit

      - name: Compute target tag
        id: tag
        env:
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          REF_NAME: ${{ github.event.ref }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [[ "$EVENT_NAME" == "pull_request" ]]; then
            target="pr-${PR_NUMBER}"
          else
            target="branch-${REF_NAME//\//-}"
          fi
          # Defense in depth: fail closed if the computed tag does not match
          # the documented handoff-tag regex. Release tags (`<version>`) and
          # `buildcache` MUST be unreachable from this code path.
          if [[ ! "$target" =~ ^pr-[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ ! "$target" =~ ^branch-[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::computed tag '$target' does not match handoff-tag regex; refusing to proceed"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "target=$target" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Computed target tag: $target"

      - name: Resolve and delete GHCR version
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          TARGET_TAG: ${{ steps.tag.outputs.target }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The package is user-owned (gmeligio); /user/packages/... is the
          # authenticated-user endpoint. The workflow GITHUB_TOKEN can delete
          # because the package -> repo Actions Access role is Admin.
          version_id=$(gh api \
            "/user/packages/container/${PACKAGE_NAME}/versions" \
            --paginate \
            --jq ".[] | select(.metadata.container.tags[]? == \"${TARGET_TAG}\") | .id" \
            | head -n 1)

          if [[ -z "$version_id" ]]; then
            echo "tag not found, nothing to delete (tag='${TARGET_TAG}')"
            exit 0
          fi

          echo "Deleting version_id=${version_id} tag=${TARGET_TAG}"
          status=$(curl -sS -o /tmp/delete-body -w '%{http_code}' \
            -X DELETE \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer ${GH_TOKEN}" \
            -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json" \
            -H "X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2022-11-28" \
            "https://api.github.com/user/packages/container/${PACKAGE_NAME}/versions/${version_id}")

          case "$status" in
            204)
              echo "Deleted ${TARGET_TAG} (version_id=${version_id})"
              ;;
            404)
              echo "Version ${version_id} already gone (404); treating as idempotent success"
              ;;
            *)
              echo "::error::DELETE returned HTTP ${status} for version_id=${version_id}"
              cat /tmp/delete-body
              exit 1
              ;;
          esac
